reviews.text: skill tree capped ruins the whole point of the game

Here is everything you need to know in under 4 min: https://youtu.be/UwVfir2RijI I know short gameplay time, but i played before. If you don''t want to watch: Fun Gameplay Twist: This game combines creature-collecting with bullet-hell mechanics in an interesting way. It’s fast-paced, which keeps things exciting, but it can feel repetitive over long sessions. Also feels a bit easy early on. I could unlock many talents after my first run. Co-op Mode Adds Value: Being able to play with up to three friends adds a lot to the experience. Working together and planning different strategies for your Tems can be rewarding, though it might feel a bit chaotic at times. Evolving Tems Mid-Run: You can evolve Tems during each run, which is a cool mechanic and lets you mix up strategies on the fly. It’s not groundbreaking, but it keeps each run feeling fresh. Boss Fights Are Hit or Miss: Some boss fights are intense and challenging, but a few feel predictable once you’ve figured out the patterns. Overall, it’s a solid mix, though some may find it lacking in variety. Content in Early Access Feels Limited: The game currently has seven Tems, 10 mini-bosses, and 5 final bosses. It’s about 60% of what’s planned, so there’s definitely more to come, but it may feel a bit thin for now.

[h1]意想不到的幸存者游戏[/h1] [quote]关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/36224058/]老实人鉴赏家 [/url] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/laoshirenLSR]老实人评测[/url]：独立游戏爱好者聚集地，黄油绅士交流中心。 不错过游戏的亮点，不放过游戏的槽点，带给玩家最直观的测评感受。[/quote] 吸血鬼幸存者大火后，类幸存者游戏犹如雨后春笋一样在steam一个个不停的冒了出来。不止小制作组想要在这个新兴的品类中分一杯羹，许多老牌工作室也积极的把自家ip和幸存者结合，像是Ghost Hhip就推出了《深岩银河幸存者》，还有著名黄油发行商神乐也推出了《神乐幸存者》，不但可以利用幸存者引流吸引新玩家注意自己的ip也可以留住喜欢幸存者玩法的粉丝，属实是一举两得了。 [h1]回合制也做幸存者?[/h1] 但《Temtem》推出类幸存者游戏还是让我大吃一惊，毕竟《Temtem》不像后来者帕鲁那样是即时战斗的玩法走的还是传统的回合制路线，一款回合制养成游戏怎么想都感觉和类幸存者没什么关系。不过仔细品味后发现制作组端上来的并不是蹭热度强行推出的游戏，确实是经过了仔细打磨的十分优秀的幸存者游戏，抛开ip来看也称得上幸存者中出类拔萃的作品。 [h1]小清新的画面[/h1] 游戏第一眼吸引到我的还是画面，继承了《Temtem》清新的画面，画质算不上高，但是让人看上去就感觉很舒服，配合不同角色各自不同的属性特效，妥妥的算是类幸存者中画面的第一梯队水平，特别是鸭嘴兽的水波特效大招，以角色为中心向四周扩散每次放都感觉十分的丝滑。而其他像是火属性电属性的技能特效也都有各自的特色，每次解锁了新的角色都迫不及待的换上看看技能与特效，也是吸引我的一大动力。 [h1]经典战斗但进化[/h1] 战斗就是标准的类幸存者玩法了，自动攻击打败敌人并不断拾取经验来升级，直到坚持15分钟击败boss，在有限的时间内尽量多的提升等级来应对关底boss。不过除了升级获取新的技能与升级技能等级外本作还加入了《Temtem》的进化机制，一旦达到特定的等级每个腾兽都可以进化两次，精华后可以全面提高所有属性，并且外形也来了个大变样，看着腾兽从小小一只和普通小怪一样大小慢慢进化成和小boss一样体型的大只佬也是非常有感觉的。坚持到15分钟后的关底boss也是气势十足，不但提醒巨大，而且每个都有好几种不同的技能，每个技能放起来基本都是占据了大半屏幕配合后期铺天盖地小怪，没有发育好的情况下还真不好打过。 [h1]总结[/h1] 作为一款ea阶段游戏本作的完成度做的还算不错，不过后续还会加入更多的地图与腾兽技能 ，妥妥的杀时间利器，不过中文翻译方面偶尔会出现有些描述还是英文有点难受。喜欢幸存者的玩家一定不要错过这款，对于《Temtem》的粉丝也可以来尝试一下这种新的类型的游戏。

It's a Pokemon themed Vampire Survivors clone with almost none of the depth of play or freedom of player expression. Impossibly curated and on-the-rails in a genre that is known for outrageous builds that can wipe the screen without you even moving. Lets say you want to unlock a new character. That's great. If you go into the menu, it doesn't tell you how to unlock any of them. If you want to do that, you have to go into the convoluted and overlapping path of exile style web of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to figure out which level and which exact attack you have to be using to unlock a new egg. The information isn't hidden or a secret, it's just presented to the player in the absolute worst and least intuitive way that is possible. The only way that simple information could be harder to acquire is if you had to use console commands. The achievements in general are bad, copy pasted entire lists of "do x damage" and "get the synergy" achievements that award nothing and reward nothing. You can change builds, elements and playstyles completely and you're always playing in the exact same way. The aura skills don't allow you enough damage instances to use them as a coherent build. Some skills don't even do damage and just block projectiles, which is great until you can't do enough damage to the boss because you needed a projectile shield to survive the level and the boss charges at you at five times your speed and stacks instances of 50% of your hp in damage on you repeatedly. Just being able to purchase characters with the global currency Pansuns would add a huge amount to letting players do what they want to do and not forcing them to playstyles they don't even like to play for 15 minutes to 2 hours of their limited human life. This is the type of game you play when you can't muster the energy to do anything else, because basically anything else in the genre would be more compelling, more rewarding, and would let you play how you want to play and make that style feel different from all the others. If you have a favourite character you can play them and still unlock stuff, you're not forced into tedious cycles of rubbing your belly while patting your head in order to play, or forced to use mathematically inferior options and handicap yourself so you can unlock the next inferior option. Game needs a lot of work. The graphics are fine. The programming has never skipped a beat. But to actually sit there and play and enjoy this title takes an extraordinary amount of effort. The 1.0 release looks like it will have about 10 characters that all feel very similar but throw a purple projectile instead of a brown one, with the elements themselves seeming to serve no purpose except to reference Pokemon. This is compared to Vampire Surivors, which has like 100 characters, many of them controlling and playing totally differently to others. The blueprint is there. It costs 5 bucks. I don't know how you could mess this up so badly. Ultimately, you could spend 5 bucks and get better than this game in this genre. You're not hurting for options in terms of survivors-likes and this one isn't one of the best. It's cute. It's fine. But ultimately, it's mediocre and doesn't differentiate itself even from joke titles. It's just bland. Like a cup of room temperature water. It's not offensive it's just.... There.

Played around five games of this genre and watched many others. Dmd, Vampire-/Soulstone/Crafty- Survivors, Holocure, etc. In its current state this is by far the worst I have played. 1. Build variety. Every character has a few skill which basically all are summed up as deal DMG in an AOE with the damage and the area values varying. That's it. Crafty Survivors went great length to give each character a unique feel and encourages builds by making the abilities interact with each other. Most interesting ability in this game was a DMG-AOE which does not appear randomly on the map, but behind your temtem this time, revolutionary. 2. Skill trees are unimaginative. CTRL+C and CTRL+V skill trees. Increase Armor, Health, Damage, Elemental Damage or other attributes for each temtem. Even though the skilltree is the same for each temtem you need to upgrade each individually, discouraging you from trying different temtem. While Soulstone-Survivors has a similar system lategame every personal skilltree has global effects, making the investment worth it. Besides soulstone survivors skill tree having unique mechanics in the tree not just +5% stat A. 3. Punishing players by unlocking new temtem. The entire enticing factor of these games is the progression, you getting stronger. This game forces you to go back the beginner level upon unlocking a new character to do its quests so you can get the skills and techniques you want on the temtem you actually put your resources into. Effect: You don't look foward to unlocking new content. 4. There are multiple stats for characters. All of them besides offensive and especially movement speed are useless. If you are not faster than even the most baby beginner enemy it walks on top of you and you die to it in one second, dealing 10% of your health every 0.1 second. There is however the heavy tank character having around 4-5 times as much armor as the rest, he only dies in 2 seconds with no chance to escape. All in all this game is very basic for its genre. If you asked an AI to extract the elements common in every Vampire-Survivor like game, the resulting mechanics would be 98% this game has to offer. Looking at their roadmap I do not really see a lot of changes to the build variety and the problems I felt this game has. Can personally only recommend this for temtem fans that want to check out the vampire survivors genre. Otherwise there are more polished and unique games out there.

Other Bullet Heaven games let you grow strong enough for whatever you fight inside the round, which obviously becomes easier with more game knowledge you have. Possibly worst developers I have come across. The game is in EA and therefore beta. I wanted to test an RNG feature of the game so I used a cheat to give myself double exp. What I found was that even doubling my levels I was not able to get a piece of gear essential for evolving a specific technique. Let me repeat; using all rerolls blocks and getting over DOUBLE the normal level was not enough to get a necessary piece of gear. I reported to the Devs that their RNG balance was skewed. They said that they would ignore my feedback because I used a cheat (except of course that cheat wasn't sufficient to fix an innate problem with their game design). If the Developers do not want people testing the limits of their game mechanics they do not deserve people playing their games and quite frankly should give up developing them. I could also talk about other issues with the game; too many skills that do NO damage that will completely brick a run; essential unlocks that are not given explanations in game that needed to be looked up online (destroying an enemy that only appears randomly on the first stage which I completed on my first run no cheats and therefore missed for most of the gameplay). However what is the point of providing feedback to a developer that wont listen and will ignore feedback. I am going to blacklist this dev from now on.

Crema has the problem that they quit obviously do not play there own games or just have absolutely no idea what makes a good game. Both temtem and temtem swarm started out as quit enjoyable and promising games that just needed a bit more to become really good. They then dedicate every update to make the game significantly worse. Grind is a problem in both of their games. A little bit is not that problematic but they for some reason seem to think that players should dedicate multiple years to these games, it is insanely slow, and restrictive in this regard. For temtem swarm specifically there is also a problem with bloat for level up rewards. There are technigues (attacks) and gears (passives) that you can randomly get during each run. The amount of different attacks and passives were already massively bloated and made t hard to get anything usefull or things that can synergize (i am not talkning about their fusion mechanic but about the general meaning of that word), to counter that they gave us a pitifull amount of rerolls and blocks that already were not enough before they introduced more passives and neutral attacks (can be obtained by any temtem) and then they also made it possible for temtem to aquire attacks (and passives) from other elements besides theyr own, an upgrade you need to take for prestige runs. There are many more problems (unclear rules, stats not explained, no real info about certain stats or how they change during a run, ...) but the two above are the most annoying for me rigth now.

得益于前作的建模基础，画风相当不错，搭配很多，技能变异相当有意思。 剩下的是缺点：1.肝，非常肝，每一个精灵升满都是单独的技能点，当然如果你只喜欢玩其中的一两个其实就还好 2.单人build相当难凑全，根据我的体感，没选但是有用技能/道具刷过了就很难重新刷出来，听牌的现象相当普遍，多人这种现象就少一些 3.但是多人联机延迟很高，相当卡，导致一些非打怪的任务根本没法完成（躲避球、冲刺之类的） 4.任务难度和奖励不对等，高难度要是刷几个难做的任务直接就崩了，恶性循环没法玩 5.精灵技能之间的强度差距实在太大，有些有清屏大的无脑强（鸭鸭变色龙），有些大招跟没有一样（电子耳），但是为了全解锁得捏着鼻子玩，很坐牢，有些技能相当强（水刃风刃等），单体群体都有相当可观的输出，有些技能甚至打不到人（触手）6.有一些怪的设计相当恶意，瞬移自爆怪，霸体自爆怪，爆完还在脚底拉一大坨，在延迟高的情况下遇到这种怪真的恶心的不行，估计做游戏的自己都没玩过几把，可能他觉得自己设计得可有意思了。 如果以上的缺点都能接受，现在30off值得一买。

TL;DR: Lacking QoL features like showing informations on items whilst having item pollution for picks up, meta-progression feeling like a counter-point due to bad techniques and gears provided during level... defensives feeling like it was added just because they seem to have needed to add defensives to the game, making offensive techniques that much better... Really wouldn't recommend Temtem: Swarm, initially it feels polished, responsive, and nice to play, but the further you get into the game, the more you realise that the game is set up in a rudementary way... the further you get into the game, the worse it gets. For example, you unlock more meta-progression, which is nice... only to get a bigger downside of techniques and gears, both of which are horribly managed... for example, getting defensive techniques are nigh useless, and just generally better to get offensive techniques... because the slower you kill, the more enemies that come... the less useful your defensives will be... thus making the meta-progression feel like a counter-point to your progression... Generally speaking... there really should just be a shared meta-progression tree... instead of giving each temtem their own skill tree... with the same extra skill tree upgrades... like the pickup distance, rerolls, snooze, and banning techniques and gears... it's all just a grind for what you basically did on your initial temtem. Lastly... the game is so hesitant about giving information to the player... like the total damage of a skill, synergies for the current selected gears and techniques... unless you're on the level up screen...general lack of information for items, and how frequent items drops... the worst items being... an individual pickup for both meta-progression currency and experience points... why have two types of map-wide pickups...? It's just an item pollution just for the sake of it...

They frequently do updates if any bugs are found which is already a huge + Having read other reviews i do want to clarify some things about stuff you can do in-game. 1. Prestiging a Tem allows you to unlock a color variation(LUMA) of said Tem when clearing a stage after you prestiged (Think of it like a shiny pokemon). This unlocks Luma spawns that drop extra EXP and can drop extra RE-ROLLS. This also unlocks a global passive for all your other tems and a personal passive for the tem making it stronger. 2. Prestiging further unlocks a second color variation that is basically a dark version of said tem that again unlocks spawns that again give more EXP and more SNOOZES or BLOCKS. Doing this also increases the bonus of the personal passive you unlocked upon prestiging for the first time. So if you keep prestiging the bonus only get's bigger and bigger as far as i know. i Havne't seen a max yet on any of my tems. 3, CO-OP adds more enemy spawns so it can make things a bit harder if you want a bigger challenge on max difficulty on the hardest map or any map you are currently on. Abilities can be used to work as a team depending on how you look at it, When you do 60min or longer runs for example, Kinu for heals , Pigepic to revive people and push back enemies and then 1 flex spot for whatever you want. This will all make sense if you play the game. Besides all this ranting, just have fun!

It is with a heavy heart that I leave a negative review for Temtem: Swarm. At the start, the game is actually a blast. Playing the early stages, progressing, and feeling yourself get stronger is great. But as you get deeper into the game, a terrible design choice completely kills the momentum: progression is entirely individualized for each Temtem. When you unlock new Temtems later on, you hit a massive roadblock. The upcoming stages are naturally much more difficult, but your newly unlocked Temtems start with zero upgrades. Because you don't have enough currency to instantly upgrade them to match the difficulty of the current stages, the natural flow of the game completely grinds to a halt. This creates an awful loop where you are practically forced to stick to just one single Temtem to farm gold, just so you can fund and play the others. Or you have to use your newly unlocked Temtems in old stages earning less currency. This is incredibly frustrating, especially since there are achievements (which give currency) tied to playing with different Temtems. The worst part is that the community warned the developers about this during the Beta/Early Access. Players explicitly suggested having a shared/general skill tree alongside individual ones (specially for upgrades like choice rerolls). The devs ignored this feedback and doubled down on their vision. Unfortunately, this stubbornness turned what could have been a great game into an incredibly repetitive, uninteresting, and tedious grind. I cannot recommend it.

Solid game without much identity. This is a feeling I get quite often with survivors games. I understand numbers going up, sense of satisfaction, metaprogression and power creeping are the main loop, what keeps the games going. If the package includes nice art and graphics, that's even better. And that is what the game offers, a robust survivors experience with an impeccable technical department that, at the same time, doesn't offer anything new. I like how well it runs on my Steam Deck, the fans on the machine only need to work in heavily overcrowded areas with several attacks (they're called "techniques" here) flying at the same time. However. Having a straightforward experience is only half of the story. I need passion, I need to feel overpowered, I want to be surprised by a sidequest or a cameo or an unexpected twist... but I found none of that here. Not even weapons' fusions (called "synergies") felt like much. Catching a new TemTem too felt underwhelming. Metaprogression was dull. All the arenas had a very samey feeling, like reskins of the same layout. Also, I fell too quickly into the loop of "I'm gonna play the next run focusing on getting this or that achievement". I don't mind (I actually enjoy) grinding a little bit to get all the achievements of a game, but I also believe that comes after having enjoyed the game "organically", and here, I found myself "working" to get those achievements too quickly. Nothing I have said means this is a bad game; it is a solid survivors entry and it can be a moderately fun game you can spend some hours with or even think about going for the whole achievements' list. But I also don't think it sits on the top5 of survivors games I've played, while also being relatively more expensive, compared to some others that definitely hit all the right notes for me. I didn't dislike it, I just didn't like it enough. I do reccomend TemTemSwarm because it is an acceptable survivors game with a solid technical bill, althought it is also true that developers played it very safe and a lack of personality, where nothing about it really stands out, makes me think I won't remember much of it in a couple of weeks.

I would've liked to recommend this version of TemTem, it has very colorful art and the Tem's are cute, visually it is a polished game. Mechanically . . . a messy experience with so many inconsistencies. Honestly I'm mostly going to list cons in this review, anyway. I'll be talking about Halls of Torment and Soulstone Survivors as well. [list] [*]When you're first playing the game with Playpet, a blue platypus, you don't have a large pool of Attacks and Utilities unlocked. So the RNG pull when leveling up is something you don't notice. As you further unlock and progress Tem's you'll start to notice the RNG pull playing favoritism, it doesn't matter how much you ignore picking something it will keep coming back, over and over. The game doesn't help you prioritize filling all of your empty slots with what you want in Solo Play. A majority of the time the RNG will prioritize Utility over trying to max out the level of your Attacks. It's so annoying. Rerolls, Blocks, Snooze (save for next level up), do exist . . . however the RNG is still actively doing whatever it wants to do for that specific Tem you're playing, thus not being in your favor. Now, there's a game called Soulstone Survivor, the Dev's cleverly split Attacks and Utility RNG pools, so with a on/off toggle you can stop pulling for new Attacks and focus on upping DMG, Speed, and more. I know TemTem Swarm is more tuned for group play but that's not a excuse to have the RNG pool being so big with every Utility lumped together. [*]Mental Attacks suck. If you enjoy a high percentage of every attack missing enemies and not targeting correctly, you do you. What happened? The design of these Attacks as well just falls flat on their faces, it's terrible too play. There are Attacks in other elements as well with similar and different issues, I think this just shows- [i]not that the Dev's are bad at their job[/i], it shows how inexperienced they are at making a cohesive balance in the design of Attacks in active combat. [*]Harping on Attacks again . . . I wish every Tem simply had their own unique sets of Attack Skills. Like a Paladin class doesn't share the same set of skills as a Monk, Necromancer shouldn't play like a Druid; there needs to be very simple boundaries to make a class feel unique. The themes of the Tems get diluted as you progress, identity along with playstyle gets muddled really fast. Like why am I using these Kung-Fu like Attacks on a really fast Bird? Because of how limited in scope the game is it would've made sense to make every Tem completely unique. [*]Hey, you... Yes YOU! Do you like overall progression? You know, upping the base health and such of ANY character you play? Obtaining gear everyone can use? Sort of like Halls of Torment if you've ever played that, if not why haven't you played HoT? Anyway, general upward progression that makes the game easier and fun and overpowered because it's fun! HA-HahahaHA! Nope, not this game! You have to get the Luma skins unlocked for each Tem to get a "global bonus" never mind the fact you basically have to unlock the whole skill tree of each Tem a maximum of 3 times! EACH! < [b]Maniacal Laughter[/b] > Please ignore how the bonuses are totally not worth the effort 'cause Luma locks the currency specific to that Tem! Oh joy! You can't play that Tem to level other ones anymore! < [b]Sarcastic Clapping[/b] > I'm totally fine! [/list] Sigh . . . my closing thoughts are this game needed better core design decisions that has progression trees benefitting all Tems, probably similar to Soulstone Survivors with their Rune system and some shared utility unlocks. I also cannot ignore how every map in TemTem Swarm mechanically feels like a copy paste with a new look, just in general playing the game feels the same every time. The Bosses/Mini Bosses are the most interesting aspect that cause the most changes in gameplay, and maybe that's the one positive I have lol. Just expect the game to be really grindy and slow without any account progression. I'm sorry, I wish the game had more solid back-end designs like level up RNG that makes logical sense like other Survivor games. If you still want to play no one can stop you . . .
